RFPENDTC represents the last date of participation for the subject for data included in submission. This is the last date of any record for the subject in the database at the time it's locked for the submission. In case of an interim cut-off, this date will not represent the end of study participation for ongoing subjects. All collected or derived dates related to dates in events, interventions, and findings datasets must be less than or equal to RFPENDTC. For events and interventions data, study teams should consider the maximum STDTC and ENDTC variables, but NOT the DTC (even when collected) since it represents a date of reporting of the event or intervention and not the date of the event or intervention itself. The only exception is the BE domain where BEDTC should be considered (in addition to STDTC and ENDTC), since BEDTC represents the date/time of specimen collection. For findings, the maximum DTC, --ENDTC should be used with the exception of PPDTC which should not be considered as it represents the date of calculation of the parameters. Special purpose CO domain should not be considered since CODTC represents the date/time of comment and not the date/time of a subject's finding, event or intervention. Note that there may be some additional exceptions to the above, which are study specific. For example: When a study collects planned interventions, in addition to actually performed ones, then the date of the planned interventions should not be considered (PRDTC, where PRCAT contains "preplanned", would not be considered). When a subject dies, in general, the RFPENDTC should equal the date of death and if any phone call was made to the family after death and recorded in the database, then this date would not be taken into account.
